# 2 Samuel Chapter 22 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 194v–195r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_022_page_001.jpg, 2SA_022_page_002.jpg, 2SA_022_page_003.jpg, 2SA_022_page_004.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** And David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

**2** He said:
"The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer —

**3** my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge;
my shield and the horn of my salvation,
my stronghold and my refuge,
my savior — you save me from violence.

**4** I call upon the LORD, who is worthy of praise,
and I am saved from my enemies.

**5** For the waves of death encompassed me,
the torrents of destruction terrified me.

**6** The cords of Sheol surrounded me;
the snares of death confronted me.

**7** In my distress I called upon the LORD;
to my God I cried out.
From his temple he heard my voice,
and my cry reached his ears.

**8** Then the earth shook and trembled;
the foundations of the heavens quaked
and reeled, because he burned with anger.

**9** Smoke went up from his nostrils,
and devouring fire from his mouth;
coals blazed forth from him.

**10** He bowed the heavens and came down;
thick darkness was under his feet.

**11** He rode upon a cherub and flew;
he appeared upon the wings of the wind.

**12** He made darkness his canopy around him —
a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

**13** From the brightness before him
coals of fire blazed forth.

**14** The LORD thundered from heaven,
and the Most High uttered his voice.

**15** He sent out arrows and scattered them;
lightning, and threw them into confusion.

**16** Then the channels of the sea were seen,
the foundations of the world were laid bare,
at the rebuke of the LORD,
at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

**17** He reached down from on high and took me;
he drew me out of many waters.

**18** He delivered me from my mighty enemy,
from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me.

**19** They confronted me in the day of my calamity,
but the LORD was my support.

**20** He brought me out into a broad place;
he rescued me, because he delighted in me.

**21** The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness;
according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me.

**22** For I have kept the ways of the LORD
and have not acted wickedly against my God.

**23** For all his judgments were before me,
and his statutes — I did not turn aside from them.

**24** I was blameless before him,
and I kept myself from my iniquity.

**25** And the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness,
according to my cleanness in his sight.

**26** With the loyal you show yourself loyal;
with the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless.

**27** With the pure you show yourself pure,
and with the crooked you show yourself shrewd.

**28** You save the afflicted people,
but your eyes are upon the haughty to bring them low.

**29** For you are my lamp, O LORD,
and the LORD illumines my darkness.

**30** For by you I can run against a troop,
and by my God I can leap over a wall.

**31** As for God, his way is blameless;
the word of the LORD is refined in the fire.
He is a shield to all who take refuge in him.

**32** For who is God besides the LORD?
And who is a rock besides our God?

**33** God is my mighty fortress,
and he sets the blameless free upon his way.

**34** He makes my feet like the feet of a deer
and sets me upon my heights.

**35** He trains my hands for battle,
so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

**36** You have given me the shield of your salvation,
and your answering has made me great.

**37** You enlarged my steps beneath me,
and my ankles did not slip.

**38** I pursued my enemies and destroyed them;
I did not turn back until they were consumed.

**39** I consumed them and shattered them so that they could not rise;
they fell beneath my feet.

**40** You girded me with strength for the battle;
you made those who rose against me bow beneath me.

**41** You made my enemies turn their backs to me,
and those who hated me — I destroyed them.

**42** They looked, but there was no one to save them;
they cried to the LORD, but he did not answer them.

**43** I ground them fine as the dust of the earth;
I crushed them and stamped them like the mud of the streets.

**44** You delivered me from the strife of my people;
you kept me as the head of the nations.
A people I had not known shall serve me.

**45** Foreigners come cringing to me;
as soon as they hear, they obey me.

**46** Foreigners lose heart
and come trembling from their strongholds.

**47** The LORD lives, and blessed be my rock!
Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation!

**48** The God who gives me vengeance
and brings down peoples beneath me,

**49** who brings me out from my enemies —
you exalt me above my adversaries;
from the man of violence you deliver me.

**50** Therefore I will praise you, O LORD, among the nations,
and I will sing praises to your name.

**51** He is a tower of salvation for his king,
and shows covenant-faithfulness to his anointed,
to David and to his offspring forever."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators recognize this as one of the great poems of the Hebrew Bible, paralleling Psalm 18 with significant textual variants. The structure is agreed upon: opening praise (vv.2-4), distress (vv.5-7), theophany (vv.8-16), rescue (vv.17-20), moral reflection (vv.21-28), empowerment (vv.29-43), dominion (vv.44-46), and closing praise (vv.47-51). Where 2 Samuel 22 and Psalm 18 diverge, all translators follow the 2 Samuel reading as the primary text. The poetic line structure and parallelism are consistently preserved across all three translations.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "spoke" vs. "sang"
- **EMET:** "And-spoke David"
- **LOGOS:** "David spoke"
- **PNEUMA:** "David sang"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "David spoke." The Hebrew uses *dibber* ("spoke"), not *shir* ("sang"). PNEUMA's "sang" is interpretive, though contextually reasonable for a song.

### V.5 — "breakers/waves of death" vs. "waves of death" vs. "waves of death crashed over me"
- **EMET:** "breakers of-death [mishberey-mavet]"
- **LOGOS:** "waves of death"
- **PNEUMA:** "waves of death crashed over me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "waves of death encompassed me." LOGOS's "waves" with the literal verb *afafuni* ("encompassed"). EMET's "breakers" is more precise for *mishberey* but less natural.

### V.5 — "torrents of worthlessness" vs. "torrents of destruction" vs. "flood of destruction"
- **EMET:** "torrents of-worthlessness [nachaley beliyya'al]"
- **LOGOS:** "torrents of destruction"
- **PNEUMA:** "flood of destruction"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "torrents of destruction." *Beliyya'al* literally means "worthlessness" but is used as a term for destructive wickedness. "Destruction" captures the contextual sense.

### V.10 — "bent" vs. "bowed" vs. "tore open"
- **EMET:** "bent [the]-heavens"
- **LOGOS:** "bowed the heavens"
- **PNEUMA:** "tore open the heavens"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "bowed the heavens." The Hebrew *vayet* means "bent/inclined." PNEUMA's "tore open" is dramatic but inaccurate.

### V.12 — "booths" vs. "canopy" vs. "tent"
- **EMET:** "booths [sukkot]"
- **LOGOS:** "canopy"
- **PNEUMA:** "tent"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "canopy." The Hebrew *sukkot* literally means "booths/shelters," but "canopy" (LOGOS) best conveys the image of darkness as God's surrounding shelter in English poetic context.

### V.17 — "sent from the height, he took me" vs. "sent from on high and took me" vs. "reached down from on high and seized me"
- **EMET:** "He-sent from-[the]-height, he-took-me"
- **LOGOS:** "He sent from on high and took me"
- **PNEUMA:** "He reached down from on high and seized me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "He reached down from on high and took me." PNEUMA's "reached down" vivifies the verb; LOGOS's "took" is more accurate than "seized" for *yiqqacheni*.

### V.27 — "twisted" vs. "shrewd"
- **EMET:** "you-show-yourself-twisted [titappal]"
- **LOGOS:** "you show yourself shrewd"
- **PNEUMA:** "you prove shrewd"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "you show yourself shrewd." The Hebrew *titappal* is from the root meaning "to twist/wrestle." "Shrewd" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) better captures God's ability to outmaneuver the devious without implying moral deficiency in God.

### V.31 — "refined" vs. "tested in the fire" vs. "flawless"
- **EMET:** "refined [tserufah]"
- **LOGOS:** "refined"
- **PNEUMA:** "tested in the fire"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "refined in the fire." Combines EMET/LOGOS's root word with PNEUMA's metallurgical context, which is inherent in the Hebrew *tserufah*.

### V.36 — "your answering" vs. "your willingness to answer"
- **EMET:** "your-answering [va'anatekha]"
- **LOGOS:** "your answering"
- **PNEUMA:** "your willingness to answer"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "your answering." EMET/LOGOS are closest to the Hebrew. PNEUMA expands beyond the text.

### V.43 — "ground them" vs. "ground them to powder"
- **EMET:** "I-ground-them like-[the]-dust"
- **LOGOS:** "I ground them fine as the dust"
- **PNEUMA:** "I ground them to powder, fine as dust"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I ground them fine as the dust of the earth." LOGOS's phrasing is closest to the Hebrew structure.

### V.51 — "tower" vs. "tower of victory" vs. "tower of salvation"
- **EMET:** "tower [migdol] of-salvations [yeshu'ot]"
- **LOGOS:** "tower of salvation"
- **PNEUMA:** "tower of victory"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "tower of salvation." The Hebrew *yeshu'ot* means "salvations/deliverances." PNEUMA's "victory" narrows the meaning.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
